react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms (RaMP multi-DB ORA, MetaboAnalystR PSEA, and Mummichog m/z-direct activity) converged on two distinct biological themes. The dominant signal is Phase I xenobiotic metabolism: RaMP ORA ranked 'Phase I - Functionalization of compounds' (REACT:R-HSA-211945, FDR = 0.0015) and 'Biological oxidations' (REACT:R-HSA-211859, FDR = 0.0021) as the top two hits, with coumarin (C05851) and putrescine (C00134) as the overlapping driver metabolites. The Mummichog empirical-compound network independently surfaced 'Xenobiotics metabolism' (p = 0.018) as a top-four hit, confirming that the same two compounds drive a drug-metabolism signal across an orthogonal m/z-directed paradigm. The second theme centers on polyamine homeostasis: RaMP returned 'Agmatine biosynthesis' (REACT:R-HSA-351143), 'Metabolism of polyamines' (REACT:R-HSA-351202), and 'PAOs oxidise polyamines to amines' (REACT:R-HSA-141334) — all driven exclusively by putrescine. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently returned hsa00480 'Glutathione metabolism' (p = 0.052) as its top hit, within which putrescine occupies the shared nitrogen-handling module, providing a second independent confirmation that polyamine flux is altered. Spironolactone (C07310) is captured by a dedicated drug-specific SMPDB pathway ('Spironolactone Action Pathway', FDR = 0.004), consistent with its known mineralocorticoid-receptor antagonism and off-target CYP interactions. CDP (C00112) independently surfaced via Mummichog in pyrimidine metabolism (p = 0.044), a plausible secondary effect of altered nucleotide demand. InChIKey reconciliation confirmed all nine input metabolites are structurally distinct (9 unique block-14 keys), ruling out namespace artefacts. The convergence of Phase I oxidative metabolism, polyamine interconversion, and a drug-specific action pathway points to a treatment that perturbs both xenobiotic clearance capacity and nitrogen/amino acid routing, with coumarin and putrescine as the key signal compounds.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms identified two convergent biological themes. RaMP multi-database ORA ranked Phase I - Functionalization of compounds (REACT:R-HSA-211945, FDR = 0.0015) as its top hit, driven by coumarin and putrescine. Biological oxidations (REACT:R-HSA-211859, FDR = 0.0021) was the second-ranked hit with the same two metabolites. Mummichog m/z-direct activity independently ranked Arachidonic acid metabolism (MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism, p = 0.0176) as its top hit, with 20-Hydroxyeicosatetraenoic acid as the signal compound. FELLA random-walk-with-restart errored at runtime and was unavailable. Cross-paradigm consensus is absent at the pathway level; the two paradigms capture distinct biological axes. RaMP additionally captured polyamine metabolism (Agmatine biosynthesis, PAOs oxidise polyamines to amines, Interconversion of polyamines, Spermidine and Spermine Biosynthesis, Metabolism of polyamines, all at FDR = 0.0041) centred on putrescine, a spironolactone-specific SMPDB hit (Spironolactone Action Pathway, FDR = 0.0041), and GABA metabolism via putrescine. Mummichog also captured N-Glycan biosynthesis and Xenobiotics metabolism (driven by coumarin and CDP).

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms (RaMP multi-DB ORA, MetaboAnalystR PSEA, and Mummichog m/z-direct activity) converged on two distinct biological themes. The dominant signal is Phase I xenobiotic metabolism: RaMP ORA ranked 'Phase I - Functionalization of compounds' (REACT:R-HSA-211945, FDR = 0.0015) and 'Biological oxidations' (REACT:R-HSA-211859, FDR = 0.0021) as the top two hits, with coumarin (C05851) and putrescine (C00134) as the overlapping driver metabolites. The Mummichog empirical-compound network independently surfaced 'Xenobiotics metabolism' (p = 0.018) as a top-four hit, confirming that the same two compounds drive a drug-metabolism signal across an orthogonal m/z-directed paradigm. The second theme centers on polyamine homeostasis: RaMP returned 'Agmatine biosynthesis' (REACT:R-HSA-351143), 'Metabolism of polyamines' (REACT:R-HSA-351202), and 'PAOs oxidise polyamines to amines' (REACT:R-HSA-141334) — all driven exclusively by putrescine. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently returned hsa00480 'Glutathione metabolism' (p = 0.052) as its top hit, within which putrescine occupies the shared nitrogen-handling module, providing a second independent confirmation that polyamine flux is altered. Spironolactone (C07310) is captured by a dedicated drug-specific SMPDB pathway ('Spironolactone Action Pathway', FDR = 0.004), consistent with its known mineralocorticoid-receptor antagonism and off-target CYP interactions. CDP (C00112) independently surfaced via Mummichog in pyrimidine metabolism (p = 0.044), a plausible secondary effect of altered nucleotide demand. InChIKey reconciliation confirmed all nine input metabolites are structurally distinct (9 unique block-14 keys), ruling out namespace artefacts. The convergence of Phase I oxidative metabolism, polyamine interconversion, and a drug-specific action pathway points to a treatment that perturbs both xenobiotic clearance capacity and nitrogen/amino acid routing, with coumarin and putrescine as the key signal compounds.
